recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-12277; any future Device.type cardinality change should come from a new OO decision that explicitly revisits FHIR-20578 and the current multiple-type guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-12277 was a Published/Persuasive OO change request raised in DSTU2 and applied for DSTU2. It asked to change Device.type to 0..1 because a Device can still be useful when the type is unknown but manufacturer, model number, or other instance details are known.
initial_application: No local source commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-12277 was found. Historical Device spreadsheet source immediately before the later FHIR-20578 application shows Device.type already at 0..1, matching the published FHIR-12277 resolution and indicating that the older request had been reflected in pre-current source.
additional_context: Later Published/Persuasive with Modification issue FHIR-20578 explicitly changed Device.type from 0..1 to 0..* for multiple distinct device type concepts, with the definition limited to types that apply to the specific device instance. Commit a7f2575daae7bbacd9a22ea439c7ec35a4784f96 lists FHIR-20578 in preapplied Device changes and changes the Device.type spreadsheet row from 0..1 to 0..*; commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 preserved those semantics in the current XML StructureDefinition source. FHIR-32562 later clarified multiple Device.type repetitions. The combined branch already contains audit commits for FHIR-20578 and FHIR-32562.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit for FHIR-12277. Device is active in source/fhir.ini, and source/device/structuredefinition-Device.xml currently has Device.type min 0 and max * with multiple-type definition/comment text. Reverting to 0..1 would contradict the later published OO decision.
